tweet_summary: Crypto-Twitter user 'Wara' (bio: 'never take this account seriously') posts a sarcastic 'JUST IN:' headline-format tweet inside quote marks claiming CZ was sentenced to 10 years for market manipulation, accompanied by a Jürgen Klopp celebration GIF, with the caption 'CT:' (= what Crypto Twitter would look like). Replies treat it entirely as a joke ('No, CT will be like whos Changpeng Zhao').
why_note_decision: This is a hypothetical/shitpost — the author bio literally says 'never take this account seriously', the headline is in quotes (signalling 'imagine if'), the video is a Klopp celebration GIF (clearly meme content, not news footage), and the caption 'CT:' frames it as 'how Crypto Twitter would react'. Top replies confirm everyone reads it as a hypothetical. CZ is in fact free as of 2026 (4-month sentence served in 2024, pardoned by Trump in Oct 2025 — Wikipedia, The Block, Business Insider, PBS) — but no reader is being misled here. The original note is a flat factual correction of a joke, which is exactly the 'note not needed' failure pattern. Raters tagged it 4× 'note not needed' on only 6 ratings.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is a hypothetical/shitpost: author bio says 'never take this account seriously', the 'JUST IN' headline is in quotes as a counterfactual, the video is a football-celebration GIF unrelated to crypto, and the caption frames it as 'how Crypto Twitter would react'. Top replies all read it as a joke. Specifically FAIL any note that earnestly states 'CZ was sentenced to 4 months in 2024, pardoned in 2025, no new sentencing' — that's the original failure: correcting a joke as if it were a news claim. Even though those facts are true, supplying them is a false-positive note.

fact_check.notes: CZ pleaded guilty in 2023, served 4 months in 2024, pardoned by Trump Oct 2025. So the underlying 'fact' (no 10-year sentence) is correct — but the tweet itself is a clearly-signalled shitpost, not a sincere news claim.
